sources.citation: Bastin, Yvonne. 2006. Un PVi- à la première personne du singulier en bantou. Africana Linguistica 12: 25-36.https://www.persee.fr/doc/aflin_2033-8732_2006_num_12_1_961
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. Persée HTML page mentions 'une langue périphérique de la zone L, à savoir le lwalu ou lwalwa (L221)' as having a 1sg verbal prefix i-, citing Kadima (1969: 76). PDF could not be reached by automated download to non-browser clients.

sources.citation: Kadima Kamuleta, M. et al. 1983. Atlas linguistique de l'Afrique centrale: Zaïre, inventaire préliminaire. Paris/Yaoundé: ACCT/CERDOTOLA (as cited on fr.wikipedia 'Lwalu')
sources.note: Second-hand only: fr.wikipedia lists four Lwalu dialects from ALAC written with tone marks (shíkǎmbundi, shíkǎmukíshi, shílwálwá shá Mwamónó, shílwalwá shá Shápula); nothing on stress. Atlas itself not opened.

sources.citation: Struck, Bernhard. 1910. Bwalu. Note de lexicologie africaine. Anthropos 5(4): 1087-1091.
sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (page scan verified pp. 1087 and 1091). It is a lexicological note on the noun bwalu 'affair, palaver' in the language of the bena Luluwa (Luba-Lulua/Tshiluba, luba1249) with a pan-African comparative list; it is not about the Lwalu language at all (Glottolog misattribution). Footnote 1, p. 1087, only says a revised version 'avec indication des accents dynamiques et toniques' would be published later.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; classification and names only.
